explanation.1_auditBeforeChange: Exhaustive (rule 165 detailed_all diagnostic) score-component table on the commit-A code, best per family — TABULAR-REFERENCE: SPIRAL-n1-CW-e+0-g0.120 L=3954 m, cumulative heading 6189 deg = 34.38 half-turns, meanCurvature 0.0273 rad/m, 0 reversals, 1 hairpin run, dev 1.583 / geo 0.000 / geom 1.899 (unusedGrade 0.033 + turnFrac 0.454 + maxAccess 0.845 + headroom 0 + curvature 0.546 + reversal 0 + hairpin 0.02) = 3.482; SWITCHBACK-k1-p+0-CW-g0.120 L=3825 m, 2998 deg = 16.66 half-turns, 0.0137 rad/m, 16 reversals, 16 runs, dev 1.772 / geo 0.030 / geom 3.044 (0 + 0.157 + 1.493 + 0 + 0.274 + 0.80 + 0.32) = 4.846; SWITCHBACK-k2-p+0-CW-g0.100 L=4580 m, 6052 deg = 33.62 half-turns, 0.0231 rad/m, 33 reversals, 33 runs, dev 1.725 / geo 0 / geom 4.011 (0.167 + 0.241 + 0.833 + 0 + 0.461 + 1.65 + 0.66) = 5.737. WARPED-301: SPIRAL-n1-CCW-e+0-g0.120 38.31 half-turns geom 2.266 (curvature 0.545, reversal 0, hairpin 0.02) total 4.072; k1 best 19.42 half-turns geom 3.830 (curvature 0.233, reversal 0.95, hairpin 0.38) total 6.021; k2 best 38.37 half-turns geom 4.821 total 6.844. GEOMETRY-STRESS has no feasible candidate since 20B.2-A. The asymmetry the directive names is confirmed: the helix turns TWICE as much as the k1 switchback in absolute terms (34.4 vs 16.7 half-turns) yet its length-normalized curvature term (0.546) is the only turning price it pays, while k1 pays 1.12 through absolute reversal / hairpin counts. The largest single k1 handicap is however maxAccessRatio 1.493 vs 0.845 (cheap reach proxy), not turning.
explanation.2_coefficientChosenBeforeSensitivity: GEOM_HALF_TURN_COEF = 0.05 = GEOM_REVERSAL_COEF, fixed a priori (documented in layout/search.py before the sensitivity run): 180 deg of cumulative steering prices the same as one direction reversal, so one hairpin (180 deg + a reversal) and one helix loop (360 deg, no reversal) both cost 0.10 — symmetric by construction, not fitted to a family. It is a geometry planning proxy (not tyre / fuel / ventilation physics). Double counting: equivalentHalfTurns and meanCurvature share the cumulative-heading measurement (count vs per-metre density) and are reported as separate components; reversal / hairpin coefficients were NOT retuned.
explanation.3_sensitivity: Offline 0x / 0.5x / 1x / 2x on the exhaustive feasible sets (score additive, geometry weight 1): TABULAR winner SPIRAL-n1-CW-e+0-g0.120 at 0 / 0.025 / 0.05 (totals 3.482 / 4.342 / 5.201 vs k1 4.846 / 5.262 / 5.678); at 0.10 SWITCHBACK-k1-p+0-CW-g0.120 wins (6.511 vs 6.920) — the spiral-vs-k1 flip point is 0.077. WARPED-301 winner SPIRAL-n1-CCW-e+0-g0.120 at every tested value (flip point 0.103; at 0.10 spiral 7.903 vs k1 7.963). Per the directive the narrow band where SWITCHBACK would win is NOT used to pick the value; SPIRAL stays the winner at the chosen 0.05 and is accepted as-is.
explanation.4_goldenOutcome: No winner changes (all four SUCCESS cases keep their 20B.2-A winner; ranking heads unchanged). Totals rise by 0.05 x half-turns for every candidate: TABULAR / CUT_AND_FILL 3.4821 -> 5.2012 (geometry 1.8986 -> 3.6177, 34.38 half-turns), WARPED-301 4.0721 -> 5.9875, IRREGULAR 5.8795 -> 7.7949 (38.31 half-turns). feasibleCount 3 -> 5 on TABULAR / CUT_AND_FILL / IRREGULAR: the stage-3 proxy (a lower bound of the weighted total) now prices the half-turn term, which displaces four n2 / n1.5 helix candidates from the shortlist tail in favour of k1 switchbacks (TABULAR shortlist gains SWITCHBACK-k1-p+0-CW-g0.120, -p+20-CW-g0.120, -p+0-CCW-g0.120, -p+0-CW-g0.100; two of them validate FEASIBLE at ranks 4-5) — winnerNormal == winnerExhaustive on all 7 cases and missedFamilies drops to [] on TABULAR / CUT_AND_FILL / IRREGULAR (WARPED-301 keeps [SWITCHBACK]: its cheap-best k1 candidates still fail the detailed gates). GEOMETRY-STRESS / 307 / ACCESS-INFEASIBLE unchanged (0 feasible).
explanation.5_noFamilyBonus: No SWITCHBACK_BONUS / SPIRAL_PENALTY / family multiplier exists; the test asserts GEOM_HALF_TURN_COEF == GEOM_REVERSAL_COEF and recomputes the geometry group component by component.
